missing), so a client can render the shared Basics & Consent step from this response alone.

accepted.description: Whether any version has been accepted.

Whether the current version has been accepted. Initial registration completion requires it. A completed
registration stays complete when a later version makes this `false`; it only signals that a re-consent is
due (a future flow).

accepted.description: Whether any version has been accepted.

current.description:
Whether the current version has been accepted. Initial registration completion requires it. A completed
registration stays complete when a later version makes this `false`; it only signals that a re-consent is
due (a future flow).

missing_requirements.description:
What initial completion still needs, in form order: empty fields, and required consents not
accepted at their current version. Always empty once complete, also after a document version
change (see `consents.*.current`).

status.description:

AccountProfileUpdateRequest.description:

accept_terms.description: Accepts the current Terms of Service version. Only `true`: required consents cannot be withdrawn here (`must_be_accepted`).

date_of_birth.description:
A real calendar date, not in the future, at least 16 years ago by calendar date (`too_young`
otherwise). Cannot be changed once registration is complete (`immutable`).

full_name.description:
The person's full name (account level; not a role profile's public display name). Trimmed;
`null` clears it while registration is in progress. After completion it can be changed, not cleared.

request must have carried the lowercase hex SHA-256 of `nonce`; the raw `nonce` is sent here. Both are

EntryResponse.description: Where the authenticated user goes next. `destination` is semantic: each client maps it to its own route.

capabilities.description:
Capabilities derived from real backend state, in the client route registry's vocabulary
(`FIGHTER` once Fighter onboarding is complete, `COACH` once Coach onboarding is complete,
`GYM_WORKSPACE` while the viewer is active staff at a gym with a completed setup; any combination can
be held). A routing projection, not an authorization grant: `COACH` opens the user's own Coach
application only, and gym access is decided per gym by its path.

context.description:
The requested `context` when it was applied (a completed profile, or `gym` with the `gym_id` of a
completed gym where the user is active staff; no `intent`; registration complete); otherwise `null`.
Never stored.

destination.description:
`account_registration`: shared basics and consents (mandatory). `role_selection`: the user chooses
a journey to start. `context_selection`: the user chooses between their profile contexts (both
completed without a remembered choice, or both onboardings in progress). `fighter_onboarding` /
`fighter_home` and `coach_onboarding` / `coach_home`: a profile's onboarding, or its application
once completed. `gym_onboarding`: start Gym setup (`gym_id` null; nothing is created) or resume the
draft gym the user owns (`gym_id`). `gym_home`: the gym workspace `gym_id` (a completed gym where the
user is active staff). `gym_selection`: the user chooses among their gym workspaces
(`gym_workspaces`). `sponsor_application`: that journey's entry point; nothing is created. A client
that does not know a destination must fail visibly, never guess.

gym_id.description:
The gym `destination` refers to (`gym_home`, or `gym_onboarding` resuming a draft); otherwise `null`.
Navigation only: every gym operation authorizes the gym id in its own path (`/api/v1/gyms/{gym_id}`).

gym_workspace_count.description: How many active gym staff memberships the viewer holds (drafts included).

gym_workspaces.description:
The viewer's gym workspaces (active staff memberships), at most 25: the draft the viewer owns first,
then newest membership first. `gym_workspace_count` is the total; read the rest with `listMyGyms`.
Re-read on every resolution, so a revoked membership is gone from the next answer.

intent.description: The validated intent of this request, echoed; never stored.

mandatory.description:
`true` when the client must go to `destination` even with a safe `returnTo` in hand (account
registration, Fighter or Coach onboarding); the `returnTo` is kept and resolved again afterwards.

reason.description: Why this destination was chosen. For diagnostics and copy, not branching.

For `validation_error` it is a `ValidationErrorDetails`: `fields` maps each invalid
field to human-readable messages and `field_codes` to the matching machine-readable

info.description:
Backend API for SimpleFit Boxing: the operating system and professional network for boxing.

## Conventions

* JSON request and response bodies (`application/json`) only.
* Errors use a single envelope (`ErrorResponse`) with a stable machine-readable `code`;
  validation errors add per-field reason codes (`ValidationErrorDetails`). Clients branch
  on codes, never on human-readable messages.
* Browser clients must be on the API's CORS allow-list (explicit origins, no wildcard).
* Every response carries an `x-request-id` header; error bodies echo it as `request_id`.
* Product resources will be served under `/api/v1`. Operational, session (`/api/auth`) and viewer
  (`/api/me`) endpoints live under `/api`.
* Authenticated endpoints take `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`; see `SessionTokens`.

post.description:
Verifies the Apple identity token (RS256 signature with Apple's keys, issuer, audience, expiry, subject, and
the nonce: the token's `nonce` must be the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw `nonce` sent here) and starts a
SimpleFit session. Apple credentials are never SimpleFit credentials and are not stored.

The Apple account is identified only by its subject (`sub`): an unknown one creates a new account
(`account: created`), a known one signs in (`account: existing`). Email (including private relay
addresses) and name are never read; accounts are never linked by email.

* `unauthorized` - the token is not a valid Apple identity token for SimpleFit (no detail is given).
* `service_unavailable` - Apple's signing keys cannot be obtained or Sign in with Apple is not configured.

post.description:
Consumes the refresh token and issues a new access token and a new refresh token for the same
session. A refresh token works once: presenting a consumed token again revokes its session,
except to recover a lost response: until the new refresh token is first used, the previous one
can be presented again for a short time, which replaces the unused new token (ADR 0010).

**Transport** (exactly one):

* Mobile/body: send `{"refresh_token": "sfr_..."}`; the new refresh token is returned in the body.
* Web/cookie: send the `__Secure-sf_refresh` cookie (no body token), an allow-listed `Origin` and
  `x-simplefit-csrf: 1`; the new refresh token is set as the cookie and omitted from the body.

post.description:
Creates one planned training session for the fighter of one of the viewer's active relationships (one
session, one fighter; no group assignment). The fighter is the relationship's; no fighter or coach id is
accepted. `client_request_id` makes the create idempotent: repeating it returns the same session with `200`
and creates nothing.

* `not_found` - unknown or someone else's session or relationship, a relationship that is not active (or whose
  accepted disclosure no longer applies, for create and update), Coach–Fighter sharing not enabled, or no
  completed coach profile.

* `conflict` - `client_request_id` was already used for another relationship (`details.client_request_id:
  "reused"`).
* `validation_error` - a field is missing, invalid or unknown; `starts_at` outside the allowed window or with
  an offset that is not `time_zone`'s; `time_zone` not a known IANA zone.

`404 not_found`, as does a viewer without a completed fighter profile.

get.description:
The viewer's email identities, oldest first: addresses whose ownership was proven with a code (at email

post.description:
Adds `email` as an email identity of the signed-in account once the 6-digit code sent to it by
`requestMyEmailIdentityLink` is entered, in the same session. Nothing else changes: no account is created or
merged, no session is issued, existing Google and Apple sign-ins stay as they are, and coach invitations to the
address become visible but still need an explicit response with every usual requirement.

* `code_invalid` - wrong code (or a code for another address). After 5 wrong codes the code stops working.
* `code_expired` - the code expired, was replaced, was already used, stopped working, or was requested in
  another session: request a new one.
* `conflict` - the address is an identity of another account. It is never moved; only reachable with the
  correct code.
* `unauthorized` - the session is no longer valid (signed out or revoked).

get.description:
Resolves where the authenticated user should go next, as a semantic destination that each client maps to its
own route (never a path). The answer is derived from current state on every call and resolving writes nothing,
so repeated and concurrent calls are safe and advance on their own as registration and onboarding complete.

Order (ADR 0017 as amended by SF-51): mandatory account registration first; then an explicit `intent`
(`fighter` / `coach` lead to that profile's home when completed, otherwise to its onboarding, whatever the
other profile's state; `gym` by the viewer's real gym workspaces (SF-84): none - `gym_onboarding` to start
setup (nothing is created); only the draft they own - `gym_onboarding` resuming it; one completed gym -
`gym_home`; several - the remembered gym, or `gym_selection`; `sponsor` to its entry point); then a requested
`context` that names a completed profile, or `context=gym&gym_id=` naming a completed gym where the viewer is
active staff; otherwise the default by completed contexts (completed profiles and completed gyms): none -
resume the one journey in progress (an onboarding, or the viewer's draft gym) or choose (`role_selection`, or
`context_selection` when several are in progress); one - its home; several - the last context chosen with
`chooseMyEntryContext` while still valid, or `context_selection`. `intent`, `context` and `gym_id` are
navigation only and grant nothing; `capabilities` (`GYM_WORKSPACE` from an active staff membership at a
completed gym) is a routing projection, and every gym operation authorizes the gym in its own path. A gym id
the viewer cannot use is ignored, never reported.

* `validation_error` - `intent` or `context` is not an allowed value (`invalid_choice`); `gym_id` is not a
  UUID, missing with `context=gym` (`required`) or sent without it.

put.description:
Records an explicit choice among the viewer's completed contexts (a context switcher or the context-selection
screen): a completed profile, or (`context: gym` with `gym_id`, SF-84) a gym with a completed setup where the
viewer is active staff. With several completed contexts and no `intent` or `context`, the entry then resolves
to this context's home. The latest choice replaces the previous one, for the viewer's account on every device
and session; it is a navigation preference, never an authorization grant: it is re-checked on every
resolution (a revoked membership or an unavailable gym is ignored), and each request still names its own gym
in its path, so tabs and devices on different gyms never interfere. Resolving the entry never records a
choice.

* `not_found` - no gym `gym_id` where the viewer is active staff (existence is never revealed); nothing is
  recorded.
* `conflict` - that profile context is not completed, or the gym's setup is a draft
  (`details.setup_status: "draft"`); nothing is recorded.
* `validation_error` - `context` is missing (`required`) or not an allowed value (`invalid_choice`); `gym_id`
  missing with `context: gym`, sent without it, or not a UUID; any other field is rejected with `invalid`
  under its name.

put.description:

offered again on any client. The first outcome is final: repeating the request, or sending the other outcome
(another tab or device), returns the kept outcome with its original `recorded_at`.

* `not_found` - unknown experience.
* `conflict` - the experience is `unavailable` to the viewer (for the Fighter experiences, Fighter
  onboarding is not complete); nothing is recorded.
* `validation_error` - `outcome` is missing (`required`) or not an allowed value (`invalid_choice`).

post.description:
The explicit acceptance on the web page of an E06 link, with its token in the body. Holding the token is not
enough. The viewer must be signed in with the invited address (an email identity they verified with a code; a Google
or Apple sign-in alone does not count: add and verify the address first with `requestEmailIdentityLink`) and
have completed account registration. Nothing else is needed: no Coach or Fighter profile is required,
created or changed, and no Coach–Fighter relationship is created. One transaction re-checks the session, the
invitation and the gym, creates the active staff membership with the invited role, consumes the invitation
and records the audit events; nothing changes if any step fails. The gym then appears among the viewer's gym
workspaces; the current context is not switched. Repeating a successful acceptance returns the same
membership (`outcome: already_accepted`).


* `invitation_unavailable` (410) - not a current pending token (unknown, resent, used, declined, cancelled
  or expired: one answer for all).
* `invitation_recipient_mismatch` (403) - the viewer is not signed in with the invited address.
* `validation_error` - `account_registration` `required` (acceptance only).
* `conflict` - the viewer is already active staff of this gym (`details.staff_membership: "already_active"`);
  the invitation stays pending.
* `rate_limited` - 30 previews and answers per 10 minutes per client.
